title: How much does a trip to Greece cost? Budget guide | Grey
summary: See how much a trip to Greece costs from five regions, with flights, hotels, ferries and a budget range for each traveller. Compare your costs.
body_markdown:
Let’s say you found a return flight from Greece for $890 and started planning a week-long vacation around it. Then you check hotels on Santorini and one night costs more than you expected to spend for three nights. You quickly realise that the flight is usually the easiest part of trips to Greece to price; hotels, ferries, and how many islands you visit are where the budget moves.


A one-week trip to Greece from the United States costs roughly $1,200 to $1,900 per person on a budget, $2,000 to $3,000 mid-range, and $5,000 or more for luxury stays. Flights, island ferries, and July and August hotel rates drive most of the difference.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost? Budget range overview


A week in Greece breaks into three cost layers: getting there, sleeping, and moving around once you arrive. Return flights from the United States typically cost $700 to $1,300. On the ground, a budget traveller spends about €450 to €800 for seven nights and a mid-range traveller spends €900 to €1,500, both assuming two people share a room. Dollar totals in this article use an assumed rate of $1.10 to the euro, so adjust them if the rate has moved by the time you book.


Three choices affect a trip to Greece more than any others.


The first is season, because July and August are when rooms cost the most, and Greece also charges a higher nightly climate fee from April to October than from November to March.


The second is which island you pick: a mid-range room that costs about €130 a night on Naxos can cost €250 to €350 on Santorini in August.


The third is how many ferry hops you add, since each leg costs €35 to €108 depending on the route and vessel.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost from the USA?


Return flights from the United States cost about $700 to $1,300. Direct flights from several East Coast cities to Athens take roughly nine to ten hours, and fares sit at the top of that range in July and August. Once you land, a 3-star hotel room in Athens typically costs €70 to €140 a night, and meals run €20 to €35 a day for budget travellers or €45 to €70 for mid-range travellers who eat two sit-down meals daily. An Acropolis ticket is €30, and a flat-rate taxi from Athens airport to the city centre costs €43 during the day and €60 at night, so an Athens-only week stays near the bottom of each range.


That puts a budget trip from the USA at roughly $1,200 to $1,900 per person and a mid-range trip at $2,000 to $3,000 per person, including one island ferry trip. Because you pay for flights in dollars and for almost everything else in euros, the[exchange rate](https://grey.co/currency-converter/usd-to-eur) and any card fees apply to nearly every purchase after you land, which is why the payment section below is worth reading before you travel.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost from North America?


This section covers Canada, Mexico, and the rest of North America; US travellers should use the section above. Return flights from these origins cost about $800 to $1,400. The ground costs are the same as for any other origin: budget travellers spend €450 to €800 per week, and mid-range travellers spend €900 to €1,500 per week. That makes a budget trip about $1,300 to $2,000 per person and a mid-range trip about $2,000 to $3,100.


Currency adds a step for Canadian and Mexican travellers. Fares may be quoted in Canadian dollars or pesos, while hotels and ferries are priced in euros, and the totals here are in US dollars and euros. Check the day’s rate between your own currency and the euro before treating any total as final, because a three per cent swing on a $2,500 trip is $75.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost from Europe?


Flights from elsewhere in Europe are the cheapest in this guide, at roughly €150 to €400 return, because most European capitals have direct routes to Athens and several islands. Ground costs stay the same: €450 to €800 for a budget week and €900 to €1,500 for a mid-range week. Totals come to about €600 to €1,200 for a budget trip and €1,050 to €1,900 for a mid-range trip, shown in euros because that is how most European travellers budget. Compare with the[Europe trip cost](https://grey.co/blog/how-much-does-a-europe-trip-cost) by country.


Travellers from the eurozone don’t convert any currency in Greece, so their only extra cost is card fees if the account isn’t in euros. Travellers from the UK, Switzerland, and Poland pay a conversion fee on every purchase, which makes the card or account you choose a bigger part of the total.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost from Africa?


Return flights from Africa to Athens cost about $500 to $1,100, and most itineraries connect through a hub such as Istanbul, Cairo, or Addis Ababa, so fares vary with the route. Citizens of most African countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, and Morocco, need a Schengen visa for Greece. The application fee is €90 for adults, and applicants usually also pay a visa centre service charge and need[travel insurance](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-get-travel-insurance) with at least €30,000 in medical cover. Add those costs to your total.


Excluding the visa, a budget trip from Africa comes to roughly $1,000 to $2,000 per person and a mid-range trip to $1,700 to $2,800. Many travellers from Africa pay for flights and hotels in dollars or euros, so how you hold foreign currency before you leave matters as much as the fare.


## How much does a trip to Greece cost from South America?


Return flights from South America to Athens cost about $1,100 to $1,900 and usually include one connection in Europe, which makes this the most expensive origin in the guide. Citizens of Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru can enter Greece without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, while citizens of some other countries in the region need one, so check with the Greek embassy before you book.


A budget trip comes to roughly $1,600 to $2,400 per person, and a mid-range trip to $2,300 to $3,600 per person. With a long-haul fare as the largest line item, the biggest savings usually come from the flight date, so compare fares across several weeks before you fix your hotel dates.


## Trip to Greece cost breakdown: flights, hotels, ferries, and food


This table lists the line items behind the totals above. Prices are per person unless a row says per room, and ferry prices vary with vessel type, season, and how far ahead you book.

Return flight from the USA $700–$1,300 Top of the range in July and August


Hostel bed €20–€40 per night Around €20 in Athens, around €40 on Mykonos and Santorini

Meals €20–€35 per day (budget), €45–€70 (mid-range), €80–€120 (comfortable) Taverna dinners average €18–€35 per person

Ferry times and prices change by season and operator, so check the[official Greek tourism site](https://www.visitgreece.gr/) for island information and confirm fares with the ferry operator before you book. If you already know your hotel and ferry costs, you can[hold euros](https://grey.co/foreign-accounts) before you leave, which locks in the exchange rate for the part of your budget you can price today.


## How to budget and pay for your trip to Greece


Once the budget is set, the next cost is paying for it. Three charges matter most: your bank's[foreign transaction fee](https://grey.co/blog/avoid-foreign-transaction-fees) , the ATM operator’s withdrawal fee, and dynamic currency conversion, which happens when a Greek card terminal or ATM offers to charge you in dollars instead of euros. Decline that offer, because the conversion is usually done at a less favourable rate than your card network’s.

A fee-free travel card from your own bank may cost less on a given trip, so compare each option’s foreign transaction fee, conversion rate, and monthly fee before you choose.


## Frequently asked questions


### How much does a trip to Greece cost?


A one-week trip to Greece from the United States costs roughly $1,200 to $1,900 per person on a budget and $2,000 to $3,000 per person in the mid-range, including flights of $700 to $1,300. Ground costs alone run about €450 to €800 for a budget week and €900 to €1,500 for a mid-range week, with hotels and ferries causing most of the variation.


### Is Greece expensive?


It depends on where you go. Daily costs run from about €55 to €210 per person on the mainland and €80 to €420 on the islands, depending on travel style. Santorini and Mykonos cost the most, and a traditional taverna dinner averages €18 to €35 per person, including house wine.


### How much does island hopping cost?


Ferry fares run €35 to €50 per leg on conventional ferries and €70 to €108 on high-speed catamarans, so three to four legs cost roughly €100 to €430. Athens to Santorini costs €40 to €60 on a conventional ferry (about eight hours) and €60 to €90 on a high-speed ferry (about 4.5 hours). The best departure times can sell out on the busiest summer routes, so book early.


### When is the cheapest time to visit Greece?


November to March is the cheapest period for the nightly climate fee, which falls to €0.50 to €4 per room, compared with €2 to €15 from April to October. Room rates are also lower outside July and August, when a mid-range room that costs about €130 on Naxos can reach €250 to €350 on Santorini. Some island ferry routes run less often in winter, so check timetables before you plan an island trip.


### Do I need a visa or ETIAS for Greece?


US, Canadian, and many South American passport holders can visit Greece for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Citizens of most African countries need a Schengen visa, with an application fee of €90 for adults. The EU’s ETIAS travel authorisation, a short online application for visa-exempt visitors, has been scheduled to start in the last quarter of 2026, so check the official ETIAS website for the start date and fee before you book.


### Should I pay in euros or dollars in Greece?


Pay in euros. When a card terminal or ATM offers to charge you in dollars, known as dynamic currency conversion, decline it, because the conversion is usually done at a less favourable rate than your card network’s. Check your own card’s foreign transaction fee and ATM charges before you leave, since those are the two fees that apply to most purchases.
